questions.question: A headlight:
questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times while riding, even during the day. This is the best way to help other road users see your motorcycle.

questions.question: When consumed together, alcohol and drugs have effects that:

options.text: Are less dangerous than when either is consumed alone.
Can be stronger than when either is consumed alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when either is consumed alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Some medications become more dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel slower than 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, a motorcycle rider has an advantage over a car driver because:

options.text: The motorcycle can accelerate faster than a car.
The rider can stay in the left part of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
Motorcycles stop in a shorter distance than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider can stay in the left part of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles on your right, you can ride in the left portion of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between vehicles. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Stopping while turning is difficult because:

options.text: The leaning bike has less grip available for stopping.
The rider is usually focused on the turn, not on braking.
The brakes do not work while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leaning bike has less grip available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When the motorcycle is leaning, some grip is used for the turn. This leaves less grip for stopping.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to proceed.
Go through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: A person is considered intoxicated with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ or higher.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a person with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered intoxicated. No intoxicated person can legally operate a motor vehicle.

questions.question: To make it easier for other drivers to see you, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing while riding.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to make yourself easier to see. This works at any time of day.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cause control problems.
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes can cause problems with control. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If your rear brake locks on a good surface, keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols or words. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns of a divided roadway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Does a DOT-compliant helmet limit a motorcyclist's side vision?

options.text: Yes, it greatly reduces side vision.
No. A DOT-compliant helmet does not limit side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. A DOT-compliant helmet does not limit side vision.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet allows you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Reflective and bright-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help make riders more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce accident risk by:

options.text: Not using turn signals so you don't distract other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Being visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To prevent collisions, make yourself visible, use turn signals, keep safe distance from others, watch the road ahead, and be ready for hazards.

questions.question: Poor braking technique:

options.text: Is not a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Poor braking is a major cause of motorcycle crashes. Learning proper braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: Before turning, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Avoid sudden power changes during the turn.
Keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden power changes during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start turning. Shifting gears while turning can cause sudden power changes that may make the rear wheel skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly.

questions.question: When being passed, where should a motorcyclist position their motorcycle in the lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane. Riding closer to the passing driver creates a dangerous situation.

questions.question: At night, how can you tell if there are bumps ahead when following another vehicle?

options.text: Listen for the vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watch the vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: At night, use the vehicle ahead of you to check road conditions. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps in the road ahead.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, you need to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a higher gear.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle accelerates, shift into higher gears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead is slippery when wet.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your headlight during the day.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, stay visible to other riders. Use your signals and brake lights. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always look at the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT reduce serious injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: A sweatshirt.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather jacket or strong synthetic jacket also protects you. A sweatshirt does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean your body toward the direction of the turn.
Slow down while in the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean your body toward the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Lean your body in the direction you are turning. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: A front wheel "wobble" or shaking is usually caused by:

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight on the motorcycle.
The front wheel not being fastened correctly to the frame.
Hitting something with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight on the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. This is usually caused by wrong tire pressure, uneven weight, or unsuitable add-ons.

questions.question: You are passing parked cars on your right with no cars coming toward you. You should ride:

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars with no oncoming traffic. This helps you avoid open car doors and people stepping out between cars. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane to have more space.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Give you a way to escape if danger appears.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a way to escape if danger appears.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning:

options.text: Should only be done if it is smooth.
Is better than shifting before the turn.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it is smooth.
questions.explanation: Shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change can cause the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically based on how you usually ride.
It applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles link the front and rear brakes together when you press the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Block your side vision so you focus on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay fastened securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield has no scratches, resists breaking, allows clear side vision, fastens securely, lets air pass to prevent fogging, and fits over eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: The gearshift is located:
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.
